name: cavemio-auth-card
title: Auth card
description: Sign-in that asks one thing at a time: the email field shrinks into a chip round the address, and your server decides whether a password, a code or a link comes next.

cavemio.accessibility:
- It is one form: Enter continues from the email field and signs in from the password field. The address is a real email input (autocomplete="email", or "username webauthn" with passkeys) and stays one, read-only, while it's a chip; Change is a button at its end.
- Each step moves focus to what comes next: the password field, the first code box, or the Open inbox button. Change returns focus to the address and selects it. Every new step's title is announced in a status region.
- Errors are linked to their field with aria-describedby and the field is marked aria-invalid. The resend countdown is hidden from screen readers; the button says when it can be used.
- The card never stores the password or code and never calls a service itself.
- Inputs use 16px type on touch screens so phones don't zoom into them.
- Reduced motion changes steps in place: no shrinking frame, slides, shakes or drawing; the words still say what happened.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: onEmail
props.description: – · Asks your server what this address needs next (and sends the code or link if that's it). Throw to keep the field and show the message.

props.name: onPassword
props.description: – · Signs in with a password. Throw when it's wrong.

props.name: onCode
props.description: – · Checks a one-time code. Resolve when it's right; throw when it isn't.

props.name: onResend
props.description: – · Sends the code or link again. Without it there is no resend.

props.name: onForgot
props.description: – · Sends a password reset link; shows "Forgot password?" on the password step.

props.name: providers
props.description: – · Sign-in providers above the email field, two to a row.

props.name: onProvider
props.description: – · Starts a provider's sign-in. A redirect keeps its button spinning; a popup that resolves moves the card to done.

props.name: onPasskey
props.description: – · Shows "Sign in with a passkey" and sets the email field's autocomplete to "username webauthn" for passkey autofill.

props.name: onSuccess
props.description: – · Runs after "Signed in" has shown, e.g. to redirect.

props.name: mode
props.description: "sign-in" · Sets the default words and the password field's autocomplete.

props.name: copy
props.description: – · Words per step: email, password, code, link, reset and done.

props.name: footer
props.description: – · Under the email step: a link to sign up, terms. It folds away after the first step.

props.name: defaultEmail
props.description: – · Starts the field with an address, e.g. from an invite link.

props.name: resendAfter
props.description: 30 · Seconds before a code or link can be sent again.

useCases.title: Sign-in and sign-up pages
useCases.description: One card for passwords, one-time codes and magic links, asked one step at a time.

useCases.title: Passwordless login
useCases.description: Email a code or a link as the main way in, with no password field to fill.

useCases.title: Social login
useCases.description: Google or GitHub buttons above the email field, two to a row.

useCases.title: Invite links
useCases.description: Open with the invited address already in the field.

features.title: Your server picks the next step
features.description: onEmail answers “password”, “code” or “link” for each address, and the card moves on.

features.title: The email becomes a chip
features.description: The field shrinks round the address, and Change takes you back to edit it.

features.title: Codes check themselves
features.description: The code is sent for checking as the last digit lands. A wrong one shakes and clears, and Resend counts down.

features.title: It opens the inbox for you
features.description: A link step offers “Open Gmail”, and the same for Outlook, iCloud, Yahoo and Proton addresses.

features.title: Providers and passkeys
features.description: Provider buttons sit above the email field, and a passkey button appears when you pass onPasskey.

features.title: Any auth service fits
features.description: The card never calls a service or stores a password. Every step is one async function you connect.

states.title: email
states.description: Providers (two to a row), "or", then the email field and Continue. An address that isn't one shakes the field and says so under it; a passkey button sits under Continue when onPasskey is set.

states.title: checking
states.description: Continue morphs to "Checking" with a spinner while onEmail runs. If it throws, the field shakes ±4px, its thin line turns red and the message opens under it.

states.title: identity
states.description: The field's frame eases from full width and 40px to the address's own width and 32px, its corners to a pill, in 520ms; the address stays where it was typed. The providers fold up above it in 460ms and "Change" opens at its end 160ms later.

states.title: next step
states.description: The new step slides in 28px from the right out of a 4px blur (440ms) while the old one leaves the other way; the card eases to its new height. Change runs it backwards and selects the address.

states.title: password
states.description: A password field with a show/hide eye that swaps through a blur. A wrong password shakes the field, selects it and says why. "Forgot password?" morphs to "Sending a link" and moves on to Check your inbox.

states.title: code
states.description: The code boxes (code input): digits rise in, the row sweeps while onCode runs, a wrong code shakes and clears, a right one melts into one pill; then the card moves on. Resend counts down.

states.title: link
states.description: "Check your inbox", with "Open Gmail" (or Outlook, iCloud Mail, Yahoo Mail, Proton Mail) for addresses it knows, and "Resend in 0:28" rolling down to Resend.

states.title: providers
states.description: The pressed provider's mark gives way to a spinner while the others dim. If onProvider throws, the reason opens under the field; if it resolves (a popup), the card moves to done.

states.title: done
states.description: A ring draws itself in 640ms, then a check inside it; "Signed in". onSuccess runs 1.3s later, e.g. to redirect.
